description: Search for PATTERNS in each FILE.
BSD grep is the default on macOS and FreeBSD.
Options marked (macOS only) are not accepted by FreeBSD's grep.

option.name: --after-context
tip: Print NUM lines of trailing context after each match.
See also -B and -C.

option.name: --basic-regexp
tip: Interpret pattern as a basic regular expression.

option.name: --before-context
tip: Print NUM lines of leading context before each match.
See also -A and -C.

option.name: --binary
tip: Search binary files, but do not attempt to print them.

option.name: --binary-files
tip: Controls searching and printing of binary files.
TYPE is 'binary' (default), 'without-match', or 'text'.
Possible values: binary, without-match, text.

option.name: --byte-offset
tip: The offset in bytes of a matched pattern is displayed in front of the respective matched line.

option.name: --bz2decompress
tip: Decompress the bzip2 compressed file before looking for the text.
(macOS only)

option.name: --colour
tip: Mark up the matching text with the expression stored in the GREP_COLOR environment variable.
The possible values of WHEN are 'never', 'always' and 'auto'.
Possible values: always, never, auto.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --context
tip: Print NUM lines of leading and trailing context surrounding each match.
See also -A and -B.
The obsolete -NUM form is the same as -C NUM.

option.name: --count
tip: Only a count of selected lines is written to standard output.

option.name: --decompress
tip: Force grep to behave as zgrep.
(macOS only)

option.name: --devices
tip: Specify the demanded action for devices, FIFOs and sockets.
The default action is 'read'; 'skip' silently skips them.
Possible values: read, skip.

option.name: --directories
tip: Specify the demanded action for directories.
It is 'read' by default; 'skip' silently ignores directories, and 'recurse' reads them recursively.
Possible values: read, recurse, skip.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Exclude files matching GLOB.
If no --include pattern is specified, all files are searched that are not excluded.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --exclude-dir
tip: If -R is specified, exclude directories matching GLOB.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --extended-regexp
tip: Interpret pattern as an extended regular expression.

option.name: --file
tip: Read one or more newline separated patterns from FILE.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --files-with-matches
tip: Only the names of files containing selected lines are written to standard output.
The scanning stops on the first match.

option.name: --files-without-match
tip: Only the names of files not containing selected lines are written to standard output.
The scanning stops on the first match.

option.name: --fixed-strings
tip: Interpret pattern as a set of fixed strings.

option.name: --help
tip: Print a brief help message.

option.name: --ignore-case
tip: Perform case insensitive matching.
By default, grep is case sensitive.
-y is an obsolete synonym.

option.name: --include
tip: Only files matching GLOB are searched.
Patterns are matched to the full path specified, not only to the filename component.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --include-dir
tip: If -R is specified, only directories matching GLOB are searched.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --invert-match
tip: Selected lines are those not matching any of the specified patterns.

option.name: --label
tip: Label to use in place of '(standard input)' for a file name where a file name would normally be printed.
This option applies to -H, -L, and -l.

option.name: --line-buffered
tip: Force output to be line buffered.

option.name: --line-number
tip: Each output line is preceded by its relative line number in the file, starting at line 1.

option.name: --line-regexp
tip: Only input lines selected against an entire fixed string or regular expression are considered to be matching lines.

option.name: --lzma
tip: Decompress the LZMA compressed file before looking for the text.
(macOS only)

option.name: --max-count
tip: Stop reading the file after NUM matches.

option.name: --mmap
tip: Use mmap(2) instead of read(2) to read input.
Can cause undefined behaviour if an input file shrinks while grep is operating, or if an I/O error occurs.

option.name: --no-filename
tip: Never print filename headers (i.e. filenames) with output lines.

option.name: --no-messages
tip: Silent mode.
Nonexistent and unreadable files are ignored (i.e. their error messages are suppressed).

option.name: --null
tip: Print a zero-byte after the file name.

option.name: --null-data
tip: Treat input and output data as sequences of lines terminated by a zero-byte instead of a newline.

option.name: --only-matching
tip: Print only the matching part of the lines.

option.name: --recursive
tip: Recursively search subdirectories listed.

option.name: --regexp
tip: Specify a pattern used during the search of the input.
May be specified more than once.

option.name: --silent
tip: Quiet mode: suppress normal output.
grep will only search a file until a match has been found, making searches potentially less expensive.

option.name: --text
tip: Treat all files as ASCII text.

option.name: --version
tip: Display version information and exit.

option.name: --word-regexp
tip: The expression is searched for as a word (as if surrounded by '[[:<:]]' and '[[:>:]]').
This option has no effect if -x is also specified.

option.name: --xz
tip: Decompress the xz compressed file before looking for the text.
(macOS only)

option.name: -H
tip: Always print filename headers with output lines.

option.name: -I
tip: Ignore binary files.
Equivalent to --binary-files=without-match.

option.name: -O
tip: If -R is specified, follow symbolic links only if they were explicitly listed on the command line.
The default is not to follow symbolic links.

option.name: -p
tip: If -R is specified, no symbolic links are followed.
This is the default.

option.name: -S
tip: If -R is specified, all symbolic links are followed.
The default is not to follow symbolic links.

option.name: -u
tip: Provided for compatibility with GNU grep.
